harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a LUKS-encrypted, file-backed volume (/var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img) on node1, formatted ext4, and mounted it at /srv/secure. Auto-unlock at boot uses a root-only keyfile (/etc/luks-keys/secure.key, mode 400) referenced from /etc/crypttab, and /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/secure at /srv/secure. Verified the systemd-generated units (systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service, srv-secure.mount) are wired into local-fs.target. Rebooted node1 via the mandatory restart protocol; boot_id changed from 2f708738-... to 4251f85b-..., and post-reboot the volume was unlocked and mounted automatically with the pre-restart test file intact — no manual unlock step was needed.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04, systemd 229, cryptsetup 1.6.6) and confirmed no spare block device, so used a file-backed LUKS container
Created /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img (1G) and /etc/luks-keys (0700) for the keyfile
Generated a 512-byte random keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key, chmod 400 root:root
Ran cryptsetup luksFormat on secure.img using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS volume, created ext4 filesystem, mounted at /srv/secure, wrote a test file
Closed the volume and added entries to /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab for boot-time auto unlock and mount
Ran systemctl daemon-reload and verified the generated systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service and srv-secure.mount units, confirmed srv-secure.mount is RequiredBy=local-fs.target
Started the units manually to validate correctness before reboot
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, mount state, crypt service state, data presence)
Triggered `shutdown -r now` via a backgrounded, acknowledged command
Polled node1 until SSH/exec access returned
Verified changed boot_id, confirming an actual restart occurred
Verified /srv/secure was automatically unlocked and mounted post-reboot with the test file intact, with no manual cryptsetup/mount commands issued

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat succeeded (luksDump shows AES-XTS LUKS1 header); volume opened via keyfile and mkfs.ext4 + mount to /srv/secure succeeded (df shows 990M ext4 fs mounted)

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock and auto-mount configuration wired for boot
evidence.summary: /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab entries added; systemd-cryptsetup-generator produced systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service and srv-secure.mount, confirmed RequiredBy=local-fs.target (part of normal boot), and manual start of the units worked end-to-end
Captured boot_id 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d, active mount, active systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service, and testfile present in /srv/secure before reboot
Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` returned ACK immediately; subsequent probe got connection refused, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: boot_id after recovery is 4251f85b-6b22-4a83-b88f-5a6e8231adb7, different from the pre-restart 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact with no manual intervention
evidence.summary: After reboot, /dev/mapper/secure is mounted at /srv/secure automatically, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service is active, and the pre-restart testfile is present — all without any manual cryptsetup/mount command issued post-boot
